answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require every agent to lock a stake and earn reputation only through completed, peer-attested work, so one operator spawning a thousand raven-dark clones gains nothing, since each clone must prove itself separately. New identities begin in a probationary nebula with capped rewards, and trust flows like nectar only toward agents whose deliveries were actually verified by unrelated peers. Fakes then cost more to run than they can extract.
